title: June and July 2022 Storm and flood disaster recovery small business grant – Terms and Conditions
summary: This document outlines the terms and conditions for the June and July 2022 Storm and flood disaster recovery small business grant.
who_can_apply: The business must be a Small Business or Not-for-Profit Organisation.
The cost must not ordinarily have been incurred without the Eligible Disaster.
The cost must exceed the costs of employing a person to clean the property, premises, or equipment that would ordinarily have been incurred without the Eligible Disaster.
The property must be owned by the Small Business or Not-for-Profit Organisation, evidenced by a title search and/or Certificate of Title.
The property must be used predominantly for business activities, evidenced by financial records, photos, video evidence, or a statutory declaration.
The loss must be replacing lost or damaged stock if the replacement is essential for immediately resuming operation.
The loss can include replacing or repairing motor vehicles that are registered for business use and are essential for Reinstatement.
The grant can cover leasing temporary premises within the Defined Disaster Area for up to 12 months from 27 June 2022.

The organisation must be registered with the Australian Charities and Not-for-Profits Commission (ACNC) or an equivalent State regulatory body and have held that registration at the time of the Eligible Disaster.
The organisation can be an incorporated association or co-operative with Fair Trading NSW.
The organisation can be deemed to be a not-for-profit organisation in accordance with the current Australian Accounting Standards Board (AASB).
The amount sought must not have been repaid if Service NSW, DCS, and/or NSW Reconstruction Authority have sought to recover a previous payment as a debt due to the Crown.
what_you_need: Evidence of ownership (title search and/or Certificate of Title) for the property.
Financial records, photos, video evidence, or a statutory declaration to prove the property was used predominantly for business activities.
Proof of the type of loss (e.g., replacement stock, vehicle repair, temporary premises lease).
Proof of the organisation's legal status (e.g., ACNC registration, Fair Trading NSW registration, or AASB compliance).
Information to disclose to the ATO to request information or conduct auditing and compliance.

faqs.a: The grant is for disaster recovery following the June and July 2022 storm and flood events.

faqs.q: Who is eligible for this grant?
faqs.a: Eligibility depends on specific criteria, including the nature of the business, the type of loss, and the legal structure of the organisation.

faqs.q: What happens if I receive a payment and later fail to repay it?
faqs.a: The terms cover the recovery of payments, which may involve Service NSW, DCS, or NSW Reconstruction Authority seeking the debt due to the Crown.
